title: Failure Case Root Cause Analyzer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Attribution activity in which learners read six illustrative failure cases from AI-assisted research, in a fixed order, and commit one of six root causes for each: missing sanity check, unverified model claim, unreviewed diff, environment drift, scope too broad, or untraceable claim. Each case has one attempt; the correct cause is always revealed with the control from an earlier chapter that would have caught the failure and a one-sentence reason. The run ends with a score of n of 6, a mastery statement at 5 of 6, and a table of the six causes with their controls.

educational.topic: Root causes of failures in AI-assisted research and the controls that catch them
learningObjectives: Attribute each of six failure cases to its root cause and to the control that would have caught it, with at least 5 of 6 attributed correctly

Connect each failure to the practice from an earlier chapter that prevents it: numerical sanity checks, primary source checks, diff review, pinned environments, single-purpose skills, and claim-to-source tracing
prerequisites: The controls of earlier chapters: numerical sanity checks, primary source checks, diff review, pinned environments, single-purpose skills, and claim-to-source tracing
The section Lessons Learned and Failure Cases in Chapter 20

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; the root-cause choice is a native select element and Submit and Next Case are native HTML buttons that respond to the Tab key and Enter or Space; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or cross symbols as well as an Okabe-Ito blue and vermillion palette; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Choose a root cause
controls.purpose: Chooses one of the six root causes for the current failure case. The picked cause is outlined on the canvas. Locked after Submit.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the chosen root cause. One attempt per case; enabled only when a cause is chosen and the case is not yet answered.

controls.label: Next Case / See Score
controls.purpose: Moves to the next case after a submission. After case 6 it reads See Score and shows n of 6 correct, the mastery statement, and the table of causes and controls.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Single-attempt attribution task with immediate explanatory feedback that always reveals the correct cause, its control, and the reason
keyQuestions: What was missing that let this through?
Which control from an earlier chapter would have caught this failure?
Is the visible symptom the root cause?
commonMisconceptions: A failure is caused by the model, and so there is nothing to change in the workflow
The visible symptom is the root cause
More careful reading would have caught each failure
assessmentOpportunities: At least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the list of controls is exploration and is not evidence
